Test at summarize-step.integration.spec.ts:145-158 goes through the real ActionsService (not a raw SQL DELETE), then reruns the pipeline with the same task reworded in casing and punctuation and confirms it does not come back — this actually exercises actionContentKey's normalization (name-normalizer.ts's case/accent/punctuation folding), not just an exact-string check.

New: an empty PATCH ({}) used to unconditionally set is_user_edited=true, silently pinning an untouched AI task against future re-runs merely because the client sent a no-op PATCH. Now actions.service.ts:94 computes `changes` from whether any of the four patchable fields is present, and returns the item unchanged at line 99 when there are none, skipping the UPDATE entirely. Verified this doesn't weaken the real-edit path: the `changes` check only short-circuits when every one of content/assignee_entity_id/due_date/status is `undefined`; a real per-field PATCH (including explicit `null` to clear a field, which is `!== undefined`) still takes the write path. Covered by integration.spec.ts:160-169.

meetings-delete-maintenance.e2e.spec.ts's 'requeue' test change (loop condition `status === 'queued'` instead of `!== 'processing'`, assertion `['processing','ready']` instead of `'processing'`) is a correct loosening, not a weakened assertion — it still fails if the meeting stays `queued` past the deadline; it now also accepts that a fully-implemented five-step pipeline can race past `processing` to `ready` before the poll observes it, which is exactly what having all steps live now makes possible.

Mobile 'Việc cần làm' filters: use-action-filters-query.ts confirmed calling GET /actions/filters (single round trip for open_total + assignees + meetings) — matches the backend contract in actions.service.ts:55-77, replacing the earlier client-side assignee-summing + GET /meetings workaround the phase-13 review would have had to flag had it shipped that way.

(Fixed this round, re-confirmed.) A deleted AI action item is now recorded in action_item_dismissals and excluded from re-insertion on the next pipeline run, closing the resurrection gap flagged last round.

New, found by the coordinator during test review and fixed proactively: an empty PATCH no longer marks an untouched AI item as user-edited. Good catch — this closes a second, more subtle path to the same class of bug as the dismissal fix (an accidental no-op PATCH would otherwise have permanently pinned an AI item against every future re-run).

Unchanged from last round, accepted as-is: if the summarize step's reconciliation DELETE commits before a concurrent user PATCH's FOR UPDATE SELECT runs on the same untouched AI item, the PATCH throws itemNotFound (404) instead of applying. Traced again against the same code (only the surrounding update() gained the empty-PATCH short-circuit, not this race) — still no data corruption, still just a confusing response the coordinator has explicitly decided to accept rather than fix.
